routes_not_delivered.reason: Next.js App Router requires all dynamic segments at the same URL position to share one slug name across the whole route tree. A new [stateCode]/[geographyCode] route directly under /research/suburb/ collided with the existing [geographyCode] route at the same position (verified live: dev server threw 'You cannot use different slug names for the same dynamic path (\'geographyCode\' !== \'stateCode\')' and failed to start). Since geography_code is already globally unique (NSW postcodes 1000-2999, VIC 3000-3999, no overlap; ASGS SAL codes are nationally unique 5-digit codes), a state-prefixed path segment was not functionally necessary for correct routing — only a URL-aesthetics nicety. Given the direct conflict with 'preserve compatibility with existing URLs', the existing single-segment routes were upgraded to be jurisdiction-aware in place instead (StateBadge/jurisdiction rendering, v2 queries) rather than introducing a redundant, framework-incompatible URL shape.

charts_deferred.detail: recharts is installed and unused in the codebase; existing and new pages render sales/rent/yield trends as tables, not charts, matching the pre-existing MarketSnapshotView pattern. Adding chart visualisation was out of scope for this pass given the time budget — tables already satisfy 'label mismatched periods, don't interpolate missing observations' since every row shows its own period and confidence explicitly, with no interpolation performed anywhere in the query layer.

browser_testing.method: gstack /browse against a real npm run dev server with WAREHOUSE_PREVIEW_ENABLED=true and MULTI_STATE_RESEARCH_ENABLED=true, pointed at the warehouse-validation branch (real committed VIC + NSW data)
